- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak or use moving average of last 5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≥ 0.25) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% if price drops >5% from 30d avg.
- Model consistently overpredicts in early 30d horizon (e.g., 2023-02-15, 2023-03-10) — apply 3–5% downward bias for first 5 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.25) and price is volatile, model tends to smooth too much; use 3-day moving average or add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to capture momentum.
- If true outcome shows strong downward correction after a high, model often fails to recognize it — apply “lag correction”: subtract 1–2% for each day after peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
